mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the following 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual monetary tightening and inflationary pressure regime, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both proxies exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 m/m change < -1% AND HOUST m/m change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 50% of such co-occurring declines.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth turns negative for two consecutive months, it signals a labor market weakening that reduces consumer spending power and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < 0% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly contraction in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months, combined with a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a coordinated supply-side and labor market downturn, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12mo MA for 4 consecutive months AND UNRATE rising for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO is below its 12-month moving average for four months and UNRATE is rising for two months.
